tasks.title: Hours, minutes, seconds
tasks.statement: Write hms(d: Duration) -> String: the format «HH:MM:SS» (hours may exceed 24; drop fractions of a second).
tasks.hint: as_secs() gives whole seconds.

tasks.title: Parsing "1h30m15s"
tasks.statement: Write parse_duration(s: &str) -> Option<Duration>: the total duration from a sequence of «<number><unit>» with the units h, m, s; an invalid or empty string gives None.
tasks.hint: Accumulate digits; on a letter, multiply by the unit.

tasks.title: Duration arithmetic
tasks.statement: Write total(parts: &[Duration]) -> Duration (the sum) and average(parts: &[Duration]) -> Option<Duration> (the mean; None for an empty slice).
tasks.hint: Duration implements Sum; division is Duration / u32.

tasks.title: Safe subtraction
tasks.statement: Write remaining(deadline: Duration, spent: Duration) -> Duration: how much is left (zero if time is up), using saturating_sub.
tasks.hint: saturating_sub does not panic.

tasks.title: Seconds since 1970 to a date
tasks.statement: Write civil_from_secs(secs: u64) -> (u32, u32, u32): the year, month and day (UTC) from seconds since 1 January 1970. The "civil from days" algorithm: z = days + 719468; era = z / 146097; doe = z − era·146097; yoe = (doe − doe/1460 + doe/36524 − doe/146096) / 365; y = yoe + era·400; doy = doe − (365·yoe + yoe/4 − yoe/100); mp = (5·doy + 2) / 153; d = doy − (153·mp + 2)/5 + 1; m = mp + 3 if mp < 10, otherwise mp − 9; y + 1 if m ≤ 2.
tasks.hint: Integer arithmetic with i64; division truncates toward zero, which is what you need for positive numbers.

tasks.title: Measuring
tasks.statement: Write time_it<F: FnOnce() -> u64>(f: F) -> (u64, Duration): call f exactly once and return its result together with the duration measured through Instant.
tasks.hint: Instant::now(), the call, elapsed().

tasks.title: Safe operations
tasks.statement: Write safe_sum(v: &[i32]) -> Option<i32>: the sum with overflow checking (None if it did not fit).
tasks.hint: try_fold with checked_add.

tasks.title: Power modulo
tasks.statement: Write pow_mod(base: u64, exp: u64, m: u64) -> u64: base^exp mod m (m ≥ 1) by fast exponentiation; intermediate products in u128.
tasks.hint: Go through the bits of the exponent; u128 holds the product of two u64 values.

tasks.title: Bits
tasks.statement: Write bit_stats(x: u32) -> (u32, u32, u32): the number of ones, leading zeros and trailing zeros (x ≠ 0 is the normal case; for 0 the methods return 32).
tasks.hint: Three integer methods.

tasks.title: Power of two
tasks.statement: Write round_up_pow2(n: u32) -> u32: the smallest power of two not less than n (1 for 0). Use the method next_power_of_two.
tasks.hint: u32::next_power_of_two.

tasks.title: Gray code
tasks.statement: Write gray(n: u32) -> u32: n ^ (n >> 1), and ungray(g: u32) -> u32, the inverse transform (ungray(gray(n)) == n).
tasks.hint: The inverse: xor of all right shifts.

tasks.title: Byte order
tasks.statement: Write swap_endian(x: u32) -> u32 without swap_bytes, using to_le_bytes and from_be_bytes.
tasks.hint: Write the bytes in one order, read them in the other.

tasks.title: Integer root
tasks.statement: Write isqrt(n: u64) -> u64: the largest r with r·r ≤ n (binary search, or the isqrt method if it is available). It is tested on large values, including u64::MAX.
tasks.hint: Binary search over r; multiply in u128.

tasks.title: Rounding to digits
tasks.statement: Write round_to(x: f64, digits: u32) -> f64: round to digits places after the decimal point (round, multiplying and dividing by 10^digits).
tasks.hint: 10f64.powi(digits as i32)

tasks.title: Comparison with tolerance
tasks.statement: Write approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, rel: f64) -> bool: |a − b| ≤ rel · max(|a|, |b|, 1.0).
tasks.hint: NaN equals nothing: the comparison gives false.

tasks.title: Mean and deviation
tasks.statement: Write stats(v: &[f64]) -> Option<(f64, f64)>: the mean and the standard deviation (by the population formula, dividing by n); None for an empty slice.
tasks.hint: Two sums: of the values and of the squared deviations.

tasks.title: Distances
tasks.statement: Write path_len(points: &[(f64, f64)]) -> f64: the length of the polyline through all points in order (hypot).
tasks.hint: windows(2) and hypot.

tasks.title: Sorting with NaN
tasks.statement: Write sorted_floats(v: &[f64]) -> Vec<f64>: a copy in ascending order with NaN at the end (total_cmp).
tasks.hint: total_cmp gives a total order.

tasks.title: NonZero
tasks.statement: Write to_nonzero(v: &[u32]) -> Vec<Option<std::num::NonZeroU32>>: each number as a NonZeroU32 (None for zero).
tasks.hint: NonZeroU32::new(x) returns an Option.

tasks.title: Hash with wrap-around
tasks.statement: Write fnv1a(data: &[u8]) -> u32: the FNV-1a hash: h = 2166136261; for each byte h ^= byte; h = h * 16777619 (with wrap-around, wrapping_mul).
tasks.hint: wrapping_mul does not panic on overflow.

tasks.title: Your own generator
tasks.statement: Implement struct Lcg { state: u64 } with a function new(seed: u64) and a method next(&mut self) -> u64: state = state · 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407 (with wrap-around); the result is state >> 33. The same seed gives the same sequence.
tasks.hint: Use wrapping_mul and wrapping_add.

tasks.title: Shuffling
tasks.statement: Write shuffle(v: &mut [i32], seed: u64): shuffle in place with the Fisher–Yates algorithm and an xorshift generator: x ^= x << 13; x ^= x >> 7; x ^= x << 17 (u64, the seed is the state; replace seed 0 with 1); for i from len−1 down to 1 swap v[i] and v[x % (i + 1)].
tasks.hint: A closure next() keeps the state x.

tasks.title: Sizes in bytes
tasks.statement: Write sizes() -> Vec<(String, usize)>: pairs (name, size_of) for the types: u8, u64, char, &u8, &[u8], String, Option<u32>, Option<&u8>, (u8, u32), [u16; 5], Box<u8>, Option<Box<u8>>.
tasks.hint: size_of::<T>() for each type.

tasks.title: Field order
tasks.statement: Write packing() -> (usize, usize, usize): the sizes of three structs: A { a: u8, b: u32, c: u8 } without repr, A_C, the same with #[repr(C)], and B { b: u32, a: u8, c: u8 } with #[repr(C)]. Declare the structs inside the function or next to it.
tasks.hint: The structs must be declared before the function.

tasks.title: The same variant
tasks.statement: There is a declared enum Shape { Circle(f64), Rect(f64, f64), Dot }. Write same_kind(a: &Shape, b: &Shape) -> bool: true if the values have the same variant (mem::discriminant).
tasks.hint: discriminant values are compared with ==.

tasks.title: Bits of a floating-point number
tasks.statement: Write float_parts(x: f32) -> (u32, u32, u32): the sign (0/1), the biased exponent (8 bits) and the mantissa (23 bits) through to_bits.
tasks.hint: x.to_bits() is a u32 with the same bits.

tasks.title: State machine and mem::replace
tasks.statement: There is a declared enum State { Idle, Running(u32), Done(String) }. Write finish(s: &mut State) -> Option<u32>: if it is Running(n), replace it with Done("done in n") (n is the number, for example "done in 5"), and return Some(n); otherwise change nothing and return None. Use mem::replace.
tasks.hint: Take the value out with replace, then write the state you need.

tasks.title: Days between dates
tasks.statement: Write days_between(y1: i64, m1: u32, d1: u32, y2: i64, m2: u32, d2: u32) -> i64: how many days from the first date to the second in the Gregorian calendar (negative if the second is earlier). Tip: convert each date into a "day number" with the days_from_civil algorithm.
tasks.hint: days_from_civil: shift the year for January and February, 400-year eras.

tasks.title: Wait with a timeout
tasks.statement: Write spin_for(limit: Duration) -> bool: in a loop, check Instant::elapsed() until limit has passed; return true if at least limit really passed (always true).
tasks.hint: while t.elapsed() < limit {}

tasks.title: Seconds since 1970
tasks.statement: Write unix_now() -> u64: the number of seconds since the start of 1970 (SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)); the check requires the result to be greater than 1.7 billion.
tasks.hint: duration_since returns a Result, so unwrap.
